page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-16 is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance provisioned with high-memory allocation. It features an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor offering 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an expansive 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero GPUs bundled, and the system provides no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark analysis highlights balanced compute and memory subsystems. In CPU evaluation, stress-ng single-core performance achieved 2927.28, placing in the top 25 percent of tested machines, while multi-core throughput registered an average tier score of 23475.85. Memory subsystem evaluations reveal high throughput, with a PassMark memory score of 2956.3 positioning in the upper quartile, alongside an uncached read bandwidth of 85.94 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 48.81 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 17.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 16.38 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of strong per-thread compute performance and high memory capacity yields solid cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand specialized AVX-512 extensions or hardware accelerators. The absence of local NVMe storage requires careful consideration for disk-intensive operations. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large Redis deployments, compilation pipelines, data processing, and lightweight model inference.
